title: Pork with rice and vegetables excluding carrots, broccoli, and dark‑green leafy; soy‑based sauce

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of tender pork pieces, steamed rice and a mix of vegetables, deliberately omitting carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy greens. It is seasoned with a soy‑based sauce that adds a deep umami flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pork is one of the most widely consumed meats worldwide.
Rice is a staple carbohydrate source in Asian cuisine, cultivated in over 100 countries.
Soy sauce originated in China more than 2,500 years ago.
Excluding carrots and broccoli makes the dish lighter for those sensitive to certain fibers.
Such combinations are traditionally served at family meals and festive gatherings.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Pork provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Energy‑providing carbs
items.content: Rice supplies complex carbohydrates that release energy gradually.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Pork contains thiamine, niacin and vitamin B6, supporting metabolic processes.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The meal offers iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for immunity and bone health.

items.title: Probiotic effect of soy sauce
items.content: Fermentation of soy sauce creates beneficial microbes that may support gut microbiota.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce is salty; people with hypertension should limit their intake.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to soy products.

items.title: Proper cooking of pork
items.content: Undercooked pork can harbor pathogens such as salmonella.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Certain pork cuts can be fatty; choosing lean cuts reduces calorie density.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, mixing pork pieces with rice and vegetables. Garnish with fresh herbs (parsley, cilantro) and a splash of lemon juice for brightness. Use the soy sauce as a drizzle or a quick marinate.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared meal in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When frozen, it retains quality for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C.
